Earlier there were rumors that Apple had cancelled its all-glass iPhone project originally planned for the iPhone's 20th anniversary, but according to the latest report from Bloomberg, the related design overhaul will still launch on schedule on next year's Pro models. Details are as follows.

Bloomberg: Redesigned design proceeding as planned

Investment bank Jefferies earlier today downgraded Apple stock, citing supply chain survey results and claiming that Apple had abandoned its all-glass iPhone project planned for next year to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone's launch.

Bloomberg's latest report states that Apple is "expected to launch an iPhone Pro model next year featuring an all-new glass-centric design," adding that "both the front and back of the phone will use glass (internal codenames V73 and V74), with the glass material extending to both sides of the body, connected in the middle by a metal frame."

However, the report also noted that the project has undergone modifications since its original conception:

The report directly refutes the note issued by Jefferies earlier today, adding that "Apple's product roadmap remains unchanged."

Jefferies Report Highlights

Jefferies analyst Edison Lee said earlier today that, based on the firm's supply chain survey, the all-glass iPhone had been cancelled due to poor production yield rates.

Lee described this development as a "significant setback" for Apple's efforts to push higher-priced iPhones amid rising memory costs, and noted that cancelling the plan could affect Apple's ability to raise the average selling price and profit margins of its Pro models.

As a result, Jefferies downgraded Apple stock and further cut its target price from US$285.56 to US$263.66, having previously lowered it from US$308.92 after Apple reported its fiscal year 2026 third-quarter results on July 31 and issued a grim guidance for the fourth quarter.
